This is the Jinja2 source repo. The claim doesn't match what's actually there.

`do_attr` (the `attr` filter, `src/jinja2/filters.py:1410-1438`) calls the builtin `getattr(obj, name)` directly, not `environment.getattr()`. `Environment.getattr()` (`src/jinja2/environment.py:485-496`) is a separate method â€” it falls back to `obj[attribute]` if the plain attribute lookup fails, and returns `self.undefined(...)` instead of raising. `do_attr` doesn't use that fallback path at all: on `AttributeError` it just falls through to `environment.undefined(obj=obj, name=name)` and never tries `obj[name]`, matching the docstring's claim that `attr` looks up attributes only, not items.

So: `attr` filter â‰  uses `env.getattr`. It replicates part of that logic (get attribute, sandboxed check, fall back to `environment.undefined`) inline instead of delegating to `Environment.getattr`.

Was this meant as something to fix/verify, or were you checking your understanding of the code?
